questions.q: What is the main difference between exec form (`CMD ["node", "server.js"]`) and shell form (`CMD node server.js`)?
options: There is no functional difference, only stylistic preference
Exec form runs the command directly as PID 1, receiving signals like SIGTERM directly; shell form wraps it in /bin/sh -c, which becomes PID 1 instead
Shell form only works with ENTRYPOINT, never with CMD
Exec form is slower because it requires an extra process
questions.explain: Exec form makes the specified command the container's main process (PID 1), so it receives signals like SIGTERM from docker stop directly. Shell form interposes /bin/sh -c as PID 1 instead.

questions.q: If a Dockerfile only sets `CMD ["node", "server.js"]`, what happens when you run `docker run northbridge/catalog:1.4 node debug.js`?
options: Docker runs both commands, server.js and debug.js, at the same time
The appended command (node debug.js) completely replaces the CMD default, so debug.js runs instead
Docker refuses to start the container because CMD was already set
node debug.js is appended as arguments to node server.js
questions.explain: With only CMD set, any command appended to docker run entirely replaces it -- there's no appending behavior, it's a full substitution.

questions.q: If a Dockerfile sets `ENTRYPOINT ["node", "server.js"]`, what happens when you run `docker run northbridge/catalog:1.4 --inspect`?
options: It runs node server.js --inspect -- the argument is appended to the fixed ENTRYPOINT
It replaces the entrypoint entirely, running just --inspect as a shell command
Docker ignores --inspect since ENTRYPOINT cannot take any arguments
It fails with an error because ENTRYPOINT doesn't accept docker run arguments
questions.explain: Unlike CMD, arguments passed to docker run are appended to ENTRYPOINT rather than replacing it, so the final command becomes node server.js --inspect.

questions.q: In the combined pattern `ENTRYPOINT ["node", "server.js"]` plus `CMD ["--port=3000"]`, what does CMD contribute?
options: A completely separate command that runs after ENTRYPOINT finishes
The default arguments passed to ENTRYPOINT, which docker run can still override by supplying its own
Nothing -- CMD is ignored whenever ENTRYPOINT is also set
The base image used for the build
questions.explain: When both are set, CMD's value becomes the default arguments appended to ENTRYPOINT -- and docker run can override just those default arguments while the program itself (ENTRYPOINT) stays fixed.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge standardize on exec form for CMD and ENTRYPOINT across its images?
options: Exec form is required by Docker Hub for all published images
So that docker stop's SIGTERM reaches the application process directly, instead of going to an intermediate shell process
Exec form makes the resulting image smaller on disk
Shell form is deprecated and no longer supported by Docker
questions.explain: Exec form makes the application itself PID 1, so it receives termination signals directly -- important for a clean shutdown, which shell form (where /bin/sh -c is PID 1) doesn't guarantee.
